audit_question: Against the post-PR #55 core, are fresh cross-vendor tethering products now predominantly A/B, and do any remaining C cases expose a genuinely reusable concept rather than manufacturer wording or an evidence gap?

products.name: 15 lb Tool Tether with choke-on cinch-loop and steel screwgate carabiner, 36"
observed_public_facts: woven elasticated polyester web tether
choke-on cinch-loop with nylon cord lock
steel screwgate carabiner with self-closing gate
15 lb maximum tool weight
products.portability_gap: The current FallTech extractor recognizes the older plain 'steel carabiner' wording used by 5027B but not the screwgate variant. Supporting 5029B is vendor-extraction broadening over existing neutral connector/cinch primitives; endpoint direction must remain unknown unless stronger evidence establishes it.

products.name: 5 lb Tool Attachment with choke-on cinch-loop and steel screwgate carabiner, 5/pk
observed_public_facts: choke-on design intended for tools with existing captive eye holes
elastic cinch-loop with nylon cord lock
steel screwgate carabiner provides the tether-side connection
5 lb maximum tool weight
products.portability_gap: The post-PR #53 core already expresses captive-eye-only eligibility without widening to handles, and the attachment may provide a carabiner interface. The remaining work is FallTech ToolAttachment extraction/composition rather than a new downstream rule.

products.name: Bungee Tether Triple-Action Carabiner - 7kg / 15lb
observed_public_facts: triple-action carabiner
elasticised heavy-duty polyester webbing
wide tail loop for fastening to tools or anchor points
90 cm minimum and 1.3 m maximum length
7 kg / 15 lb rated load in the detailed specifications
evidence_notes: The current storefront summary exposes a malformed '7 g / 15 g' Max Load field while the product title and detailed specifications state 7 kg / 15 lb. Treat the malformed field as an evidence/extraction issue; do not create a new capacity semantic.
core_fit: plain loop endpoint unless separate evidence establishes a cinch mechanism
products.portability_gap: The GRIPPS adapter currently targets the H01079 directional dual-carabiner pattern and does not yet extract this carabiner-plus-tail-loop topology. The normalized core already represents the observed facts; the malformed storefront load field is an evidence-quality issue, not a portability gap.

products.name: SnapLock
observed_public_facts: self-closing tool connector creates a tethering connection point
installs to a tool handle or neck
available in small, medium, large and extra-large sizes
6.8 kg / 15 lb maximum load
core_fit: attachment_method_code = mechanical_capture is a plausible retention family
required_core_changes: define a reusable executable non-captive handle/neck capture eligibility and fit boundary without treating a size label as geometry or requiring captive state; determine from installation evidence whether fit is dimension-resolved or requires a bounded pre-use/runtime verification
products.portability_gap: The runtime feature/predicate model can describe non-captive features, but the production eligibility compiler has no conservative family for a self-closing attachment installed around a non-captive handle/neck. The next slice must not invent S/M/L/XL dimensions or reuse the captive-handle compiler.

products.name: Tool Lanyard - Carabiner and Cinch Loop - 10lbs
observed_public_facts: locking screwgate aluminum carabiner with captive eye
cinch loop end for tethering to captive holes on tools
10 lb / 4.5 kg maximum working capacity
35-45 in standard length and 42-54 in extended variant
products.portability_gap: Ergodyne requires a new vendor acquisition/extraction path, but the product's connector, cinch-loop, capacity and length facts map to existing normalized semantics without downstream changes.

products.name: Retractable Tool Lanyard - Stainless-Steel Carabiner and Loop - 2lbs
observed_public_facts: manual-locking stainless-steel carabiner is explicitly the anchoring end
choking loop is explicitly the hand-tool connecting end
retractable working range is 10 to 48 in / 25 to 122 cm
self-setting pawls can lock the retractable at a selected working length
2 lb / 0.9 kg maximum working capacity
products.portability_gap: This is a genuinely unseen Ergodyne tether family rather than the tape/wrap ToolAttachment architecture sample used before PR #55. Its explicit directional carabiner/choking-loop topology, retractable form, capacity and working-range facts fit the current neutral core; Ergodyne acquisition/extraction is the remaining work. The pawl mechanism may be preserved as product detail but does not require a new recommendation rule for this audit.

products.name: DBI-SALA D-Ring Attachment 1 in x 3.5 in
observed_public_facts: D-ring attachment creates a tool tethering point
manufacturer instructs use of Quick-Wrap Tape II to attach the D-ring to the tool
D-ring is used with Quick Wrap Tape as an attachment system
2.3 kg / 5 lb capacity
products.portability_gap: Although the required tape/wrap assembly pattern was already considered during pre-PR #55 architecture design, this 3M product does not require a new companion-product semantic: required_pairing plus a multi-component assembly can represent the separately catalogued D-ring and Quick-Wrap components. Its B classification is therefore about onboarding this manufacturer into an already-established model, not evidence of a newly discovered portability primitive.

products.name: DBI-SALA Quick Spin Medium Size
observed_public_facts: tangle-resistant spin top slides onto the handle of a tool
reusable non-conductive attachment point
2 cm / 0.8 in medium nominal size
0.5 kg / 1 lb capacity
core_fit: attachment_method_code = mechanical_capture is a plausible retention family
required_core_changes: define the same reusable non-captive capture eligibility/fit boundary exposed by GRIPPS SnapLock; nominal attachment size must not be treated as a complete tool-feature fit envelope, and snug/secure fit must remain evidence-bound
products.portability_gap: The current compiler cannot express a slide-on attachment that is intentionally retained on a non-captive handle without either falsely requiring captive state or inventing a min/max fit envelope from a nominal product diameter. This recurs independently from GRIPPS SnapLock and therefore merits one generic follow-on investigation rather than a 3M-specific rule.
